item.title: The Ant Route
item.passage: Amir and Sara watched ants crossing a dry patch of ground in the school garden. They stayed beside their teacher and kept their hands away from the insects. Sara drew a line on paper to show where the ants were going. At first, she made the line straight. Amir pointed to a fallen leaf that several ants were walking around. Sara changed her line to bend around a leaf shape. Then they noticed a second group taking a different route past a small rock. Instead of rubbing out the first line, Sara added another. By the end of their visit, the page looked like a little road map. Back in class, Amir tried following one line with his finger. He stopped at a crossing and asked which way to go. Sara laughed and said their map needed another visit before they could answer that.

questions.stem: What did several ants walk around?
questions.evidence: Amir pointed to a fallen leaf that several ants were walking around.

questions.stem: Why did Sara keep the first line?
options: She could not remember where the first route went.
She had seen more than one route being used.
She wanted the map to look like a star.
questions.evidence: Then they noticed a second group taking a different route past a small rock.
questions.rationale: The new route belongs to another group, so it adds information rather than replacing the earlier observation.

questions.stem: What is the story mainly about?
options: Guiding insects along a route chosen by children.
Making a map that shows every path in a garden.
Changing a drawing to match what is being observed.
questions.evidence: Instead of rubbing out the first line, Sara added another.
questions.rationale: Their paper develops as they notice more of the ants’ actual movements; it remains incomplete.
